open_points.subject: create replay after an ordinary change to the created record
open_points.text: This holds while the record the first create made keeps its values
open_points.question: Which changes make a record stop qualifying as keeping its values, and what happens to its create request identity after a correction, archive, restriction, relationship end or other accepted lifecycle change?
options: The original request remains associated with the record until erasure or anonymisation, so a retry is still recognised.
Any change to any fact ends replay recognition, so the same request is handled as a fresh create.
Only changes to facts supplied by the create request end replay recognition; status, revision and timestamps do not.
open_points.default_guess: Keep recognising the request while its written-once request id remains on the record; only erasure, anonymisation or deletion removes that association.

witness.initial: An active project P was created by the owner with request id R.
events: The owner corrects P's alias, moving its revision.
The owner repeats the original create request with request id R after losing its first answer.
outcomes: Registry recognises R and returns P, whose alias now has the corrected value.
Because P no longer keeps its original values, Registry treats R as a fresh create and makes a second project.
witness.observer: The owner and every consumer that later sees one project versus two.

open_points.subject: project-create replay after whole deletion
open_points.text: Erasing a customer or anonymising a project removes everything that would tell a repeat; a create repeated after that is a new create
open_points.question: Does deleting an archived project whole also remove create-replay recognition and make a later repetition a new create, or is replay information retained somewhere despite the project record being gone?
options: Whole deletion behaves like anonymisation for replay: the repeated create makes a new project.
A replay marker survives whole deletion, so the repeated create is still recognised or refused as a replay.
open_points.default_guess: Treat whole deletion like anonymisation and handle the repetition as a new create.

witness.initial: Project P was created by the owner with request id R and was later archived.
events: The owner confirms deletion of P whole.
The owner repeats the original create request with request id R.
outcomes: Registry treats the request as new and creates project Q.
Registry retains replay knowledge outside P and does not create Q.
witness.observer: The owner and consumers trying to use the newly returned project identity.

open_points.subject: project-create replay after anonymisation when current creation preconditions fail
open_points.text: a create repeated after that is a new create, and its answer shows the new record it made
open_points.question: Is a repeated project create after anonymisation still subject to the current customer eligibility checks, or must it make the new record promised here even when the original customer is now erased, restricted or ended?
options: Apply current create preconditions and refuse the repetition when its customer is no longer eligible.
The replay exception requires creation of a new project despite the customer's present state.
open_points.default_guess: Apply current create preconditions; treating the request as new should not bypass them.

witness.initial: The owner created project P linked to customer C; both were initially active and unrestricted.
events: The owner archives and anonymises P.
The owner repeats P's original create request.
outcomes: The new paragraph says the answer shows the new project the repeated create made.
The create-project action says a restricted customer reference is refused, so no project is made.
witness.observer: The owner, and any service that would later see the new project.

open_points.subject: room-create replay after project anonymisation
open_points.text: a create repeated after that is a new create, and its answer shows the new record it made
open_points.question: Does “a create” mean only recreation of the Customer or Project whose own create evidence was erased, or also a retry of a room create whose Room and request id disappeared when its project was anonymised?
options: The exception applies only to Customer and Project creates.
It applies to every erased create record, including a Room removed by project anonymisation.
A room retry is handled as a fresh attempt but refused because the project is archived and anonymised.
open_points.default_guess: Limit the exception to creation of the Customer or Project expressly named; refuse room creation on the anonymised project.

witness.initial: Active project P contains room Rm, added by the owner with create request id X.
events: The owner archives and anonymises P, removing its rooms.
The owner repeats the add-room request with id X.
outcomes: Reading “a create” broadly, Registry makes a new room and returns it.
Applying the add-room lifecycle rule, Registry refuses because P is archived and anonymised.
witness.observer: The owner and any planner or agent reading P's rooms.
